checks.name: sr_overlap
checks.why: SET and RESET must not both assert in ideal logic

checks.name: default_off_v
checks.why: power-up with POR set must leave the SR bias off

checks.name: startup_max_v
checks.why: the switch must never conduct before the first explicit reset; this run uses preinitialized latch and gate; arbitrary startup is untested. A non-zero value here may indicate a startup issue; do not dismiss it as artificial

checks.name: enabled_v
checks.why: an explicit reset with PERMIT must pass the full 15 V rail

checks.name: after_fault_v
checks.why: the fault must cut the bias, not merely lower it

checks.name: held_off_v
checks.why: with the fault gone and no reset the bias must stay off

checks.name: recovered_v
checks.why: an explicit reset must restore the bias

checks.name: latched_after_fault_v
checks.why: the latch, not the fault input, is what holds the bias off

checks.name: enable_after_fault_v
checks.why: ENABLE must be low while latched

checks.name: off_input_current_a
checks.why: the cut must remove the load current; only leakage remains

checks.name: on_input_current_a
checks.why: the enabled state must carry the bench load (~15 mA)

checks.name: gate_off_v
checks.why: R50 must hold the gate at VDD_IN with the switch off

checks.name: bias_cut_time_s
checks.why: the gate must reach 15 V - |Vth| within tens of microseconds; R50 * 60 pF says ~14 us, and anything past 40 us means the gate node is being held by something else

checks.name: discharge_time_s
checks.why: VDD_SR reaches a 3.63 V reporting threshold with the 11.1 uF equivalent bank; not a REG/gate-off guarantee

checks.name: reverse_current_a
checks.why: back-fed VDD_SR=18 V must not conduct through the switch; the only path is the R50 bleed

checks.name: reverse_vdd_sr_v
checks.why: the back-fed node holds 18 V: a conducting pass pair would drag it toward VDD_IN

stress_assessment.scope: all_checks_pass covers only the listed behavioural checks, not stress or hardware approval

note: behavioural switch and logic model; this is not a device model, not a thermal model, and not a hardware measurement
